questions.history: A new child thread publishes CustomEvent(`child`), then the parent joins it and reads the filtered stream.
questions.prediction: The parent revision is expected to record no child event. The landing should return exactly one event whose message is child.
questions.basis: The issue identifies thread-local recording as the missing link. The landed Jupiter test publishes from a new child, joins it and asserts its message.
questions.refutation: The merged test loses the child event, records it twice or changes the message.

questions.history: Publish CustomEvent(`parent`) on the recording test thread and read the filtered stream there.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should record exactly that event once.
questions.basis: Synchronous capture on the active test thread is the pre-existing feature. Filtering by class makes unrelated Spring lifecycle events immaterial.
questions.refutation: The ordinary same-thread record is absent or duplicated.

questions.history: In one test publish tag A on the parent, publish B on a fresh child and join it, then inspect the injected ApplicationEvents from a second fresh child and from the parent.
questions.prediction: On the landing both consumers should observe A then B exactly once. Both threads are created after the recorder is registered.
questions.basis: Sequential publication plus join establishes order. Two independently created children should see the recorder for their common test. This crosses both the producer and reader thread boundaries.
questions.refutation: The parent sees both tags but a child sees none, sees only its own event, or fails to resolve the recorder.

questions.history: Give a recording Jupiter test explicit @TestInstance(PER_CLASS) and @Execution(CONCURRENT) with parallel execution enabled. As a separate landing check, keep the annotations and disable global parallel execution.
questions.prediction: At the landing expect a failing container with IllegalStateException in the enabled case, as tested. The validation source predicts the same rejection with global parallelism off. The parent has no Spring guard for this combination.
questions.basis: The landed extension inspects merged class annotations and their values. Its diagnostic suggests disabling parallel execution, yet the guard does not read the global switch.
questions.refutation: The annotated class runs under enabled parallelism, or the otherwise identical globally disabled case passes despite the predicted annotation-only check.
